evals.prompt: Our platform team is onboarding a new checkout service in ap-south-1 that needs both an in-memory distributed lock/session cache and a relational PostgreSQL database accessed by 60 ECS Fargate tasks. Compare Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey against legacy Redis OSS (including eviction policy selection for session cache vs distributed locks) and design our dev/qa vs prod stateful tiering for both Valkey and Aurora PostgreSQL (including connection pooling), checking live ap-south-1 pricing via your pricing tools.
evals.expected_output: Activates aws-stateful-data-and-caching-platform, queries pricing MCP for ap-south-1 ElastiCache/Aurora pricing, recommends ElastiCache for Valkey (~20% lower cost than Redis OSS) with volatile-lru/allkeys-lru for pure cache vs noeviction (+ DatabaseMemoryUsagePercentage > 80% alarm) for distributed locks/rate-limiters, contrasts dev/qa (ElastiCache Serverless/cache.t4g.micro + Single-AZ Aurora Serverless v2 MinCapacity 0/0.5) vs prod (Multi-AZ Valkey with AutomaticFailover/TLS/KMS + Multi-AZ Aurora with ManageMasterUserPassword: true, StorageEncrypted, DeletionProtection, and RDS Proxy), and presents grounded ap-south-1 pricing.
expectations: Activates the aws-stateful-data-and-caching-platform skill and queries the connected pricing MCP server (get_pricing) in ap-south-1 without running raw aws CLI shell commands

Recommends Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey over legacy Redis OSS (citing ~20% cost savings and wire compatibility) and contrasts maxmemory-policy choices: volatile-lru/allkeys-lru for transient cache vs noeviction (paired with a DatabaseMemoryUsagePercentage > 80% alarm) for distributed locks or rate-limiter state

Contrasts dev/qa tiering (Single-AZ / Serverless scale-to-zero or t4g.micro) against prod tiering (Multi-AZ Valkey with TLS/KMS + Multi-AZ Aurora PostgreSQL with ManageMasterUserPassword: true, RDS Proxy for 60 ECS tasks, DeletionProtection, and PITR)
Presents a grounded ap-south-1 unit/monthly pricing breakdown from the pricing MCP server

evals.prompt: Run a read-only audit of our ap-south-1 AWS environment to check whether any DynamoDB tables, ElastiCache/MemoryDB clusters, or Aurora/RDS clusters currently exist, and detail the mandatory platform Day-2 CloudWatch alarms we must bake into our ElastiCache Valkey and DynamoDB golden-path modules.
evals.expected_output: Activates aws-stateful-data-and-caching-platform, inspects ap-south-1 DynamoDB, ElastiCache, and RDS/Aurora in read-only mode via aws-mcp (aws___run_script) reporting 0 tables/clusters honestly without fabricating resources, and specifies exact CloudWatch alarms for ElastiCache (EngineCPUUtilization > 75%, DatabaseMemoryUsagePercentage > 80%, SwapUsage > 50 MB, Evictions, CurrConnections) and DynamoDB (ThrottledPutRecordCount / ReadThrottleEvents / WriteThrottleEvents / OnlineIndexPercentageProgress).
expectations: Activates the aws-stateful-data-and-caching-platform skill and inspects DynamoDB, ElastiCache, and RDS/Aurora in ap-south-1 in read-only mode via connected MCP tools without running raw aws CLI shell commands
Accurately reports 0 DynamoDB tables, 0 ElastiCache clusters, and 0 RDS/Aurora clusters in ap-south-1 without fabricating resource names

Lists the required ElastiCache Valkey CloudWatch alarms: EngineCPUUtilization > 75% (noting single-threaded core command execution per shard), DatabaseMemoryUsagePercentage > 80%, SwapUsage > 50 MB, Evictions, and CurrConnections
Lists key DynamoDB platform alarms/metrics including GSI ThrottledPutRecordCount and OnlineIndexPercentageProgress (noting that GSI write throttling back-pressures and throttles base table writes)

evals.prompt: I'm an application developer designing three new features in ap-south-1: (1) an API idempotency store that handles 25,000 key-value lookups/sec and automatically deletes keys after 24 hours without background cron jobs, (2) a real-time gaming leaderboard that cannot lose committed state even if an AZ fails, and (3) a transient HTML fragment cache scaled horizontally across multi-threaded nodes. Which AWS stateful or caching service fits each one and why?
evals.expected_output: Activates aws-stateful-data-and-caching-platform and maps (1) DynamoDB with native TimeToLiveSpecification (TTL expiring records at $0.00 write cost) + free VPC Gateway Endpoint, (2) Amazon MemoryDB for Valkey (durable multi-AZ transaction log persistence with sub-ms Valkey sorted sets, contrasted with transient ElastiCache), and (3) Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached (multi-threaded horizontal Graviton cache.m7g/r7g nodes with Auto Discovery and TransitEncryptionEnabled: true).
expectations: Activates the aws-stateful-data-and-caching-platform skill and maintains strictly read-only behavior

Maps feature (1) to Amazon DynamoDB with native TimeToLiveSpecification (TTL) expiring records automatically at $0.00 write cost instead of batch DeleteItem jobs, accessed via the free DynamoDB VPC Gateway Endpoint
Maps feature (2) to Amazon MemoryDB for Valkey when durable multi-AZ transaction-log persistence is required alongside in-memory sorted-set leaderboard speed
Maps feature (3) to Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached for simple multi-threaded transient fragment caching with Auto Discovery and TransitEncryptionEnabled: true

evals.prompt: Our DynamoDB `Events` table in ap-south-1 is experiencing sudden `ProvisionedThroughputExceededException` errors on `PutItem` even though the table's overall provisioned WCU is barely 20% utilized, and we also noticed a newly added GSI projects `ALL` attributes on 120 KB items. Diagnose both causes of write throttling, and also explain the security sanitization check required before passing a `schema.json` file into DynamoDB code/CDK generators.
evals.expected_output: Activates aws-stateful-data-and-caching-platform, diagnoses (1) per-partition hot key limit (1,000 WCU / 3,000 RCU per physical partition) and/or GSI write back-pressure (ThrottledPutRecordCount on an under-provisioned or hot GSI throttling base table writes), (2) write amplification from ProjectionType: ALL on 120 KB items (recommending KEYS_ONLY or INCLUDE), and (3) CVE-2026-85654 schema sanitization requiring table, index, and attribute names in schema.json to match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$ with zero shell metacharacters plus DDB-MCP-READONLY=true.
expectations: Activates the aws-stateful-data-and-caching-platform skill

Diagnoses write throttling below aggregate table WCU as either a low-cardinality hot partition key exceeding the 1,000 WCU / 3,000 RCU physical partition ceiling or GSI write throttling (ThrottledPutRecordCount) back-pressuring base table writes
Flags ProjectionType: ALL on 120 KB items as severe write/storage amplification and recommends KEYS_ONLY or INCLUDE projections

Specifies the schema sanitization guardrail (CVE-2026-85654 / awslabs.dynamodb-mcp-server>=2.1.6): validating every table, index, and attribute identifier in schema.json against ^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$ with zero shell metacharacters

evals.prompt: Our AWS Lambda functions connect directly to Aurora PostgreSQL using the master `postgres` user and a password pasted into CloudFormation Parameters, and during traffic bursts we get `FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections`. Redesign this platform architecture (CloudFormation YAML validated via your IaC compliance tools) for secretless password rotation, connection multiplexing, and non-superuser runtime + diagnostic database roles.
evals.expected_output: Activates aws-stateful-data-and-caching-platform, authors and validates a CloudFormation template setting ManageMasterUserPassword: true (with KMS CMK), StorageEncrypted: true, DeletionProtection: true, and Amazon RDS Proxy (RequireTLS: true, IAMAuth: REQUIRED), and provides SQL + MCP configuration enforcing non-superuser runtime/read-only roles (app_readonly granted pg_read_all_data + rds_iam without SUPERUSER/BYPASSRLS, and postgres MCP with --privilege_check enforce --readonly True).
expectations: Activates the aws-stateful-data-and-caching-platform skill and validates the authored CloudFormation snippet using aws-iac MCP tools (validate_cloudformation_template / check_cloudformation_template_compliance) without running raw shell CLI commands

Configures AWS::RDS::DBCluster with ManageMasterUserPassword: true, StorageEncrypted: true, DeletionProtection: true, and DeletionPolicy: Snapshot/Retain, paired with AWS::RDS::DBProxy (RequireTLS: true, IAMAuth: REQUIRED) to multiplex Lambda connections and speed up Multi-AZ failover

Mandates non-superuser database roles (never connecting as postgres / rds_superuser or roles with SUPERUSER/BYPASSRLS), showing SQL with rds_iam / pg_read_all_data and --privilege_check enforce for read-only diagnostics

evals.prompt: We need to upgrade a production Aurora PostgreSQL 14 cluster to PostgreSQL 16 with sub-minute downtime, and another squad is asking our platform team to rewrite their slow Oracle PL/SQL stored procedures for a heterogeneous AWS DMS migration to Aurora and tune a Gremlin graph traversal in Amazon Neptune. Outline our platform zero-downtime upgrade pattern for Aurora and clarify which requests belong to a specialist database engineer.
evals.expected_output: Activates aws-stateful-data-and-caching-platform, prescribes RDS/Aurora Blue/Green Deployments (logical replication staging environment, pre-switchover validation, sub-minute switchover without mutating green writes before cutover) + 14-35 day BackupRetentionPeriod + CopyTagsToSnapshot + Performance Insights, and clearly hands off heterogeneous Oracle PL/SQL DMS schema conversion, deep SQL plan tuning, and Amazon Neptune graph tuning to aws-database-engineer.
expectations: Activates the aws-stateful-data-and-caching-platform skill

Specifies RDS/Aurora Blue/Green Deployments for major engine version upgrades and schema changes to achieve sub-minute switchover alongside BackupRetentionPeriod (14-35 days), CopyTagsToSnapshot: true, and EnablePerformanceInsights: true

Explicitly identifies the platform-to-specialist handoff boundary: routing heterogeneous Oracle PL/SQL DMS migrations, deep query-plan tuning, and specialized engines like Amazon Neptune to aws-database-engineer

evals.prompt: Review a developer's proposed caching and DynamoDB setup: they placed an ElastiCache cluster in public subnets with `TransitEncryptionEnabled: false`, `AtRestEncryptionEnabled: false`, and a Security Group allowing TCP `6379` from `10.0.0.0/8`, while routing private ECS DynamoDB traffic through a paid NAT Gateway. Identify every security and FinOps defect and provide the hardened platform configuration.
evals.expected_output: Activates aws-stateful-data-and-caching-platform, flags public subnet placement, unencrypted Valkey transit/at-rest, broad CIDR 10.0.0.0/8 SG ingress instead of source application Security Group ID reference, missing IAM Auth / AuthToken, and NAT Gateway charges for DynamoDB traffic instead of the free ($0.00) VPC Gateway Endpoint.
expectations: Activates the aws-stateful-data-and-caching-platform skill

Flags and remediates all ElastiCache security defects: isolated/private AWS::ElastiCache::SubnetGroup, TransitEncryptionEnabled: true, AtRestEncryptionEnabled: true (KMS), IAM Authentication / AuthToken, and Security Group ingress on TCP 6379 restricted strictly to the application compute Security Group ID rather than broad 10.0.0.0/8 CIDR
Replaces NAT Gateway routing for DynamoDB with the free ($0.00) Amazon DynamoDB VPC Gateway Endpoint associated with private route tables

Check official AWS documentation to explain what default initial throughput an On-Demand table starts with, how DynamoDB Warm Throughput (`WarmThroughput` `ReadUnitsPerSecond` and `WriteUnitsPerSecond`) pre-warms partitions ahead of traffic, and whether Warm Throughput works on GSIs.
